purpose: Targeted novelty and evidence-boundary audit for the pincer-catmech-ai research redesign; not an exhaustive systematic review or a Nature acceptance assessment.

hypotheses.claim: Cation-associated speciation or intrinsic hydride reactivity dominates the condition-dependent hydrogen-transfer response.
discriminating_observables: dissolved base, water and alcohol measurements
hypotheses.falsifier: Within predeclared measurement sensitivity, matched conditions remove the effect and a cation-independent model predicts held-out data equally well.
hypotheses.generic_novelty_status: already precedented by P02 and adjacent P06

hypotheses.claim: Alcohol or water primarily changes organic condensation/dehydration rather than metal hydrogen-transfer chemistry.
discriminating_observables: orthogonal isotope response with exchange checks
hypotheses.falsifier: Additive effects are absent in condensation but present in isolated hydrogen transfer and metal speciation, beyond measurement uncertainty.
hypotheses.generic_novelty_status: alcohol/water and ligand-assisted proton processes already precedented by P03, P04 and P09

hypotheses.claim: History-dependent dormant/deactivated populations or base depletion explain activity-lifetime tradeoffs.
discriminating_observables: separate catalyst and base restoration responses
hypotheses.falsifier: Within the accessible time window, instantaneous composition predicts fresh and aged systems without a history or catalyst-loss term.
hypotheses.generic_novelty_status: deactivation-aware and non-standard modelling already precedented by P07 and P10
